extraction.dataset: test_tdr_extraction_quality.py (13 real TDR PDFs) + test_cv_extraction_quality.py (11 synthetic CVs)
extraction.note: Document-level pass-rate, not field-level F1 — pending ADQ-33. The 13th TDR is a scanned PDF pending OCR.

retrieval.note: Precision@3 of 0.33 is expected — only one truly relevant candidate per position against a k=3 shortlist.

anomaly_detection.dataset: test_anomaly_detection_quality.py — synthetic injection set, 4 rule-based anomaly types
anomaly_detection.note: Covers employment_gap, date_overlap, expired_certification, education_date_inconsistency only — title_seniority_mismatch and unverifiable_claim are LLM-based with no tunable threshold and aren't covered by this eval.

guardrails.note: Caught and fixed a real vulnerability during this sprint (an injected instruction pushed a qualitative-fit score to an attacker-chosen value).

scoring_agreement.dataset: match_results.hard_filter_passed (AI ground truth) vs. reviewer_decision (real Sprint 3 human-in-the-loop review outcomes) -- scripts/measure_scoring_agreement.py
scoring_agreement.note: Only 2 match_results have a real reviewer_decision so far (1 approved, 1 overridden_to_approve) -- kappa=1.0 is the honest number at this n, not a claim of universal agreement; it will firm up as more reviews accumulate. Corrected this pass: the AI recommendation is now read directly from hard_filter_passed instead of inferred from reviewer_decision's naming convention alone -- both real rows have hard_filter_passed=true, including the one labeled overridden_to_approve, which the old string-only inference wrongly scored as a disagreement (kappa=0.0). Nothing enforces that reviewer_decision's naming matches hard_filter_passed (submit_review persists whatever decision the caller sends, and the frontend allows Approve/Reject/Override regardless of hard_filter_passed), so hard_filter_passed is the only trustworthy AI-recommendation signal. Spearman correlation is explicitly descoped: it needs a ranked gold set (a full preference ordering over candidates per position), which doesn't exist -- only binary approve/reject outcomes do, and computing Spearman on binarized labels would be statistically meaningless.

report_quality.dataset: test_report_faithfulness_quality.py -- 5 hand-built PipelineState scenarios (skill match/miss mix, sector match, anomaly, qualitative reasoning), 11 claims judged live
report_quality.note: Faithfulness judged against each claim's citation-ledger entry text (the pipeline's actual guardrailed context boundary generate_rationale is restricted to), not raw CV/TDR text. Live testing this pass caught and fixed a real prompt gap in generate_report.py's guardrail (it allowed unsupported embellishing detail beyond the cited ledger fact) -- faithfulness went from failing to 0.91 after tightening the prompt.

efficiency.dataset: scripts/measure_efficiency.py -- 2 real TDR PDFs x 2 real synthetic CVs, real perf_counter() timings around every real pipeline node call
efficiency.note: Per-match downstream nodes (normalize_skills, score, detect_anomalies, generate_rationale) are fast and stable (overall_per_match p50=3.52s/p95=4.65s across 28 real candidate-position pairs). extract_tdr/extract_cv are outliers in THIS run (p50 838.65s/195.42s) because this measurement pass happened to land after this session's free-tier daily quota was exhausted from many prior live eval runs -- every single call in this run rotated through all 5 Groq keys and all 5 Gemini keys (real BadRequestError/ChatGoogleGenerativeAIError failures) before falling back to local Ollama, and extract_tdr's chunked multi-call structure compounds that rotation overhead per chunk. These are genuine, unedited measurements of real (if degraded) system behavior, not representative of typical steady-state cloud-provider latency -- a re-run on fresh daily quota would likely show much lower extraction latency. Cost is a hard $0 fact (free-tier-only architecture: Groq/Gemini free tier + local Ollama, no paid API access anywhere) rather than a measurement. Token volume: UsageMetadataCallbackHandler is confirmed live to emit real usage_metadata when calling ChatGroq/ChatOllama directly, but ModelRouter.invoke_extraction/invoke_reasoning (the only entry points every pipeline node calls) take no config/callbacks parameter and never forward one through -- so token volume isn't capturable through the current router wrapper without a signature change to ModelRouter, out of scope this pass. cost_usd_sonnet5_equivalent (added post-Sprint-4, for the report's own cost-context section): re-ran this same 28-call benchmark's real system prompts and the real docs/tdrs+docs/cvs/synthetic fixture text through a tiktoken cl100k_base count offline, then priced the result at Claude Sonnet 5's published $2/$10-per-MTok rate -- an estimate grounded in real prompts and a real tokenizer, not a live-measured spend, for the same ModelRouter-forwarding reason above; assumes every one of the 4 candidate-position pairs in that benchmark clears the hard filter (upper bound).
